items.title: EPSS Surge: CVE-2026-4408
items.analysis: EPSS exploitation probability for CVE-2026-4408 surged from 0% to 47% (percentile 99%), indicating a significant increase in predicted or observed exploitation activity for this 2026-era vulnerability. It is not (yet) in CISA KEV — this signal typically precedes KEV listing and press coverage. A flaw was found in Samba. A remote attacker can exploit a misconfiguration in Samba file servers and classic domain controllers that use the "check password script" feature. If this script is configured with the %u substitution character, the client-controlled username is passed without proper escaping of shell meta-characters. This vulnerability allows an attacker to achieve remote command execution on the affected system. This issue primarily affects non-standard configurations where the "check password script" is used with %u and the samba-dcerpcd service is started as a system service.

items.title: EPSS Surge: CVE-2025-68645 (Zimbra Collaboration)
items.analysis: EPSS exploitation probability for CVE-2025-68645 surged from 49% to 51% (percentile 99%), indicating a significant increase in predicted or observed exploitation activity for this 2025-era vulnerability. It is not (yet) in CISA KEV — this signal typically precedes KEV listing and press coverage. A Local File Inclusion (LFI) vulnerability exists in the Webmail Classic UI of Zimbra Collaboration (ZCS) 10.0 and 10.1 because of improper handling of user-supplied request parameters in the RestFilter servlet. An unauthenticated remote attacker can craft requests to the /h/rest endpoint to influence internal request dispatching, allowing inclusion of arbitrary files from the WebRoot directory.

items.title: EPSS Surge: CVE-2019-12527
items.analysis: EPSS exploitation probability for CVE-2019-12527 surged from 49% to 50% (percentile 99%), indicating a significant increase in predicted or observed exploitation activity for this 2019-era vulnerability. It is not (yet) in CISA KEV — this signal typically precedes KEV listing and press coverage. An issue was discovered in Squid 4.0.23 through 4.7. When checking Basic Authentication with HttpHeader::getAuth, Squid uses a global buffer to store the decoded data. Squid does not check that the decoded length isn't greater than the buffer, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow with user controlled data.
